name: Corporate Credit Tradelines Builder
tag: A step-by-step plan for building business credit that stands on its own, apart from your personal credit.

scenarios.title: Start credit for a new LLC
scenarios.ask: My LLC is {months} months old with {done} of the 6 foundation items in place. Build my tradeline plan.
steps: Foundation check
Reviewed the 6 basics: EIN, business bank account, business address, business phone, business credit bureau profiles and matching records. {=6 - done} still open.
Vendor planner
Picked {=2 + pace} starter vendor accounts that sell on net-30 terms and report payments to business bureaus.
Payment scheduler
Set reminders to pay each invoice early, since on-time history is what builds the file.
Timeline
Mapped tiers: starter vendors, then store accounts, then fleet and cash cards.

result.title: Your tradeline plan
rows: Estimated weeks to first reported history
Timelines vary; no approval is guaranteed

followups: Lenders and bureaus check that your business name, address and phone match everywhere. Mismatches are a common reason applications stall, so the {=6 - done} open items come first.
Yes. Many lenders look for time in business. At {months} months, starter vendor accounts are the right first step, and larger lines usually come later.

scenarios.title: Separate business and personal credit
scenarios.ask: Our {accounts} business accounts include {guarantees} with a personal guarantee. Show how to separate them.
steps: Account reader
Listed all {accounts} accounts with limits, balances and who is on the hook.
Guarantee check
Flagged {=min(accounts, guarantees)} accounts tied to you personally.
Reporting check
{=min(accounts, personal)} accounts report balances to your personal file, which can raise your personal utilization.
Plan writer
Ordered replacements: open business-only accounts first, then move spending and close or downgrade the tied ones.

result.title: Separation plan
rows: Educational plan, not legal or credit advice

followups: Can I remove a personal guarantee?
Sometimes. Some lenders will release it once the business shows enough history and revenue. The plan lists which accounts to ask about first.
Should I close old accounts right away?
Usually not. Closing accounts can affect credit history. The plan moves spending first and closes accounts only when replacements are in place.

scenarios.title: Get ready for a bigger credit line
scenarios.ask: We want a ${target} business line. We have {lines} tradelines reporting and ${revenue} in monthly revenue.
steps: Profile reader
Pulled the sample business file: {lines} tradelines reporting, all paid on time.
Lender match
Compared the ${target} target with typical lender rules of thumb, such as a line near 10% of yearly revenue.
Gap finder
Listed what is missing: more tradelines, time in business or revenue history.
Plan writer
Wrote a 90-day checklist to close the gaps before applying.
followups: Why tie the line to revenue?
Lenders want to see that you can repay. Many start near 10% of yearly revenue, which is about ${=round(revenue * 12 * 0.1)} for you. Rules differ by lender.
What raises the readiness score fastest?
Adding reporting tradelines and paying them early. Revenue history grows more slowly, so the plan works on both at once.
